evidence.effect: Rest-of-day to last half-hour momentum (ROD -> LH), Russell 2000 futures
evidence.rule: r_ROD = P(LH start = 15:30 ET)/P(prior close 16:00 ET) - 1; regress r_LH on r_ROD (trade: sign of r_ROD, hold 15:30-16:00 ET)
evidence.conversion: beta 6.00 (x100): about 6.0 bp of LH return per 1% of r_ROD = 12 M2K ticks per 1% at L=2,000. Per-trade mean needs mean |r_ROD| for ER, not reported; not derived. M2K: $5 x index, tick 0.10 pt = $0.50 (CME filing ptc041519cmedcm003 lines 125, 161). 1 bp of notional = L x 1e-4 pt = L/1000 ticks; at L = 2,000 (Russell 2000 first above 2,000 on 2020-12-23, Wikipedia) 1 bp = 2 ticks = $1; range over the search window about 1,500-2,400 gives 1.5-2.4 ticks per bp.

proposed_features.name: fomc_r1
proposed_features.source: Gao, Han, Li, Zhou (JFE 2018; Dec 2015 WP read), Table 8 Panel B and Sec. 3.1
proposed_features.quote: Release            FOMC           20.04**               5.84             3.43 | rule: 'we will take a long position in the market at the beginning of the last half-hour if the timing signal is positive, and take a short position otherwise ... the position (long or short) is closed at the market close' | r1: 'we calculate the first half-hour return using previous day's close price and the price at 10:00am Eastern time'
proposed_features.formula: On RTY rows of trade date d: if d is a scheduled FOMC statement date in the FOMC calendar (E.14 2010-06-01..2019-05-31; frozen release calendar 2019-05-01..2026-06-21, release FOMC), value = close(bar b_{08:59 CT}, the bar closing 09:00 CT on d) / close(bar b_{C-1}, closing at C_X = 15:00 CT on the previous trade date of the equity group calendar) - 1, applicability flag 1; otherwise value 0, flag 0. Direction used by the paper: sign(value). Not applicable when the previous date is an early-halt date (no C_X close, as G5) or when either bar is absent (missing, row excluded).
calendars: FOMC statement calendar: reports/stage_e14_cal_releases.json (FOMC rows) and reports/stage_e2b_release_calendar.json (FOMC rows)
proposed_features.derivation: Published: 20.04%/yr on FOMC-day trades, annualized like a daily return, so 20.04/252 = 7.95 bp per trade gross (SPY, LH 15:30-16:00 ET, 1993-2013, about 165 events, t 2.46). M2K ticks per bp = L/1000: at L = 1,500 / 2,000 / 2,400 that is 11.9 / 15.9 / 19.1 ticks; D8 RT 6.346 ticks ($3.17), ratio 1.88 / 2.51 / 3.01. Caveats that lower the expectation: (a) SPY, not Russell (Gao Table 12: IWM's unconditional first-half-hour effect is larger than SPY's on the same mean-variance method, 11.72 vs 6.85 %/yr, different samples); (b) t4 with h60 = F holds 14:09-15:08 CT, 59 minutes, not the paper's 14:30-15:00 CT, and includes 15:00-15:08 after the cash close; (c) no post-2013 test of the FOMC interaction; the ONFH form weakens out of sample in later work (Baltussen Table B1 ES R2_OOS -1.68%; Rosa 2022, NQ reader) and the related pre-FOMC drift 'essentially disappeared after 2015' (Kurov et al. 2021, abstract only); (d) about 15 FOMC dates in RTY's backward window (2017-07-11..2019-05-05) and 37 in the search window; (e) the paper calls the dates 'FOMC minutes' while giving statement timing.
